A narrow left margin holds one note in small italic, beside entries 27 and 28, and a bullet mark. Running head "NOTÆ." at the top, page number "60" at the top left, catchword at the foot of the column.

main_text.p: 24 شمر يرعش[?] Shamr Yaraasb i. e. Shamer qui tremit, tremens à tremore qui ipsum occupaverat denominatus. Nisheri filius, vel juxta alios Africi, ab eo Samarcandam nomen traxisse volunt.
25 ابو مالك[?] Abu Malec, Shameri filius.
26 عمران[?] Amran, Ameri filius, è posteris Cahlani, translato tunc imperio à posteris Hamyari, ad posteros fratris ipsius Cahlan. fuit Amran iste كاهنا[?] Hariolus.

27 عمرو بن عامر[?] Amrus filius Ameri, cui cognomen مزيقيا[?] Mazikia, quasi Dilacerator dicas, inditum, quòd binas quas quotidiè induebat, vestes, vesperi dilaceraret, eas vel ipse rursum induere, vel ut ab aliis induerentur, pati dedignatus. v. Aljau-harium & AlFirauZabadium, &c.AbulFeda paulo aliter, quod se. quoties in publicum prodiret, novam assumeret vestem lacerata priore.
29 ذو حبشان[?] Dhu Habshan, Akrani filius, atque hic est qui Tasinum & Jadisum (ut perhibent) è medio sustulit.
31 كليكرب[?] Colaicarb, (vel ut AlJannabium, & Ahmed Ebn Tusef. مليك يكرب[?] Molaic Tacrab, Tobbai filius.

32 ابو كرب اسعد[?] Abu Carb Asaad, qui تبع الاوسط[?] i. e. Tobbaa medius, cujus in Alcorano mentio, 700. ante Mohammedem annis floruisse perhibetur, ac primus Caaba aulaea circumdedisse, Ejus suasu ac ignis, quem in rebus dubiis consulebant كاهنا[?] quod qui falsum praetenderet, consumere soleret; qui verum diceret, intactum relinqueret indicio, Hamyarenses ab Idolorum cultu ad Iudaismum converfi, atque inde fuit اصل اليهودية في اليمن[?] Iudaismi

page.notes: Arabic words transcribed from the scan without full vowel marks; those with [?] are doubtful. The Arabic in entries 24 and 26 to 32 is hard to read at this resolution. Catchword "Iudaismi" is read from the foot of the column and is uncertain. The left margin note is in small italic, positioned beside entry 27. Long s is printed throughout and is transcribed as s.
